title: A day in the life of an industrial designer running collaborative design reviews, without endless revision cycles
summary: See how industrial designers use Unity Studio to streamline collaborative design reviews, reduce redesign cycles, and align stakeholders faster with interactive 3D workflows.
body_markdown:
***Disclaimer: This story features a fictional persona created for illustrative purposes and does not depict a real customer or individual.***


Elena has spent the last seven years designing products that balance aesthetics, functionality, and manufacturability.


She loves solving design challenges. What she enjoys far less is explaining those designs.


Not because the work isn't clear, but because once a design leaves her CAD software, it often loses the context that made it make sense in the first place.


By 9:00 am, Elena is already reviewing feedback from three different teams.


Engineering wants to revisit the shape of the front bumper to improve manufacturability. Marketing thinks the latest wheel design doesn't quite reflect the premium look the brand is aiming for. Leadership wants confidence the latest vehicle concept is ready for an executive design review.


And somewhere between screenshots, PDFs, email threads, and annotation tools, the original design intent is starting to get lost.


Again.


For industrial designers, this is one of the most frustrating parts of the job.


Not designing the product.


Not solving technical constraints.


But navigating the endless cycle of fragmented feedback, differing interpretations, and costly redesigns that happen when stakeholders can't fully experience a design.


Because static images can only communicate so much.


That’s why Elena started using[Unity Studio to run interactive design reviews](https://unity.com/products/unity-studio) .


Instead of relying on screenshots and disconnected review workflows, she can now create interactive review environments that stakeholders explore directly in the browser, helping everyone discuss the same design from the same perspective.
